snippet.title: 3D SCANNING With Your PHONE - to create a GAME LEVEL | Display.Land // Maya // UE4
snippet.description:
In this sponsored video I look at 3D scanning using a smart phone - also known as photogrammetry - using Display.Land, a cool app that turns your scans into detailed and fully textured 3D models. The app is available on both iPhone and Android. To test out the app I quickly and easily scan some objects in a forest and then use them to create a level in Unreal Engine 4 - after some optimization in Maya. This was a fun video to make - hope you enjoy it :)

Check out Display.Land for free here: https://displayland.app.link/GameDevAcademy
You can also check out their youtube channel, DisplaylandHQ here: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCd8I46id4VBXBTJ8ySb4KmQ

If you want to continue learning about 3D scanning and photogrammetry, get a *free 10 day trial to Pluralsight* and check out the course I mentioned in the video here: https://pluralsight.pxf.io/Wk7k3

snippet.title: How to Fix Messy Topology FAST Using Maya 2020
snippet.description:
In this short video tutorial, I show you how to use the retopologize tool in Maya 2020 to correct any messy topology you may have in your 3D models. This is really powerful for restoring edge flow, quadrangulating your mesh and for redistributing geometry evenly. Give it a try!

snippet.title: Unreal Engine 4 Blueprint Tutorial for Beginners
snippet.description:
In this free Unreal Engine 4 for beginners tutorial video you will learn everything you need to know to create your first game in Unreal Engine 4. Topics covered include setting up a project, adding inputs for controlling the game - including touchscreen controls, using Blueprints, importing art assets, using destructible meshes and adding audio. By the time you have completed the exercise you will have created a fully working castle themed Breakout game!

♥ You can access the assets used for this tutorial here: https://gumroad.com/l/AVmjX

♥ This tutorial builds upon many of the skills covered in my previous Unreal Engine 4 for Beginners tutorial which you can access here: https://youtu.be/a0qNO6_xPx0

♥ This tutorial has been made freely available on YouTube because I believe that quality education should be freely available to everyone. Want to support me in my mission?

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 12 The completed animation
snippet.description: Your animation is now complete. Well done! Make sure that you show off your work by posting a video reply to this video or by posting it on the facebook page!

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 11 Make your walk cycle loop using graph editor
snippet.description: In this step you will use the graph editor to loop your animation. This means adjusting the post infinity of your curves to cycle. You will use cycle offset for the movement of your lamp.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 10 Move lamp forward by animating another group
snippet.description: In this step you will once again use a group to allow you to animate the lamp moving forward.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 9 Animate the head of the lamp using FK
snippet.description: You will now use forward kinematics again to allow you to animate the head of your lamp.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 8 Add rotation to animation to simulate momentum
snippet.description: You will now use another group to allow you to animate the rotation of your lamp. This will make it look like you lamp has some momentum as it moves.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 7 Animate the base with forward kinematics
snippet.description: Now that your lamp jumps up and down you will use forward kinematics to animate the base. This will make it look like the lamp is putting some effort into jumping along.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 6 Make the lamp move up and down using grouping
snippet.description: You will now add your lamp and rig to a new group before using it to add the height to your animation.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 5 Animate the arm of the lamp using IK effector
snippet.description: You will now begin animating your lamp by using the IK handle you created earlier.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 4 Attach the mesh to your skeleton using parenting
snippet.description: In this step you will attach your lamp to the skeleton by using parenting.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 3 Add a skeleton using joint tool
snippet.description: In this step you will use the joint tool to create a skeleton for your lamp. You will then create an IK effector for this rig using the IK handle tool.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 2 Model the lamp using polygons
snippet.description: In this step you will quickly create a lamp for you to animate.

snippet.title: Animation in Maya 2015 - Rig and animate a lamp - 1 Concept
snippet.description:
In this series of videos you will learn the basics of rigging a model for animation using both forward and inverse kinematics in Maya. For this exercise you will create and animate a lamp like the one used by Pixar, Luxo Junior.

This first video introduces the project and the concept of rigging models for animation.

To complete this tutorial you need Autodesk Maya. Follow this link to learn how to get Maya for free - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n_SjClie5bw

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 15
snippet.description: Now that your scene is full of little fires you need to make the background look like it is being illuminated by these fires.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 14
snippet.description: In this step you will duplicate the fire and smoke to make the scene look more action packed.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 13
snippet.description: In this step you will create the fire which is the source of the smoke that you added in the previous step. You will also add colour to the smoke to make it look like the fire is illuminating it.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 12
snippet.description:
In this step you will add some smoke to the image. This involves resizing and rotating the image. You will then erase some of the smoke to make sure it blends with the rest of the background.

You'll then need to correct the colours of the smoke using a range of adjustment layers and clipping masks.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 11
snippet.description: In this step you will create a lake using a colour blending layer.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 10
snippet.description: With the rocky terrain created you will now correct the colours of the rocks you have imported to match with the rest of the image.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 9
snippet.description: This step is all about reusing the stock image we imported to create the rocky terrain we need for the image. You can use your own creativity to complete this step.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 8
snippet.description: In this step you will first put down a background colour for the ground part of the image. You will then import part of another stock image to create the rocky terrain.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 7
snippet.description: In this step you will adjust the colour of the new part of the sky a little further. Once this is done you will put all of your sky layers into a group or folder.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 6
snippet.description: As we did in the previous steps we will now correct the colours on the new bit of sky we have brought in using adjustment layers and clipping masks. This time we will use a colour balance adjustment layer and a hue and saturation adjustment layer.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 5
snippet.description: In this step you will create a new levels adjustment layer. You will then create a clipping mask for this layer. You will then add another part of the sky image using the stock photos.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 4
snippet.description: In this step you will use the clone stamp tool to make the sky a little more interesting. You will then create a new gradient map adjustment layer to further change the colours of the sky

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 3
snippet.description: In this step you will create a clipping mask to allow you to desaturate (make black and white) part of the sky.

snippet.title: Create a war scene with stock images - Photoshop CS6 tutorial - Part 2
snippet.description:
In this step you will import and image for the sky background. This will involve using the free-transform tool.

You will then erase some of the sky using the eraser tool with a soft brush setting.

snippet.description: In this step you will repeat the process of preparing the mesh to extrude a wing. This time you will prepare to extrude the back wings.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 16 - Round out the wing
snippet.description: In this step you will insert a new edge loop and use this to make the wing smoother and rounder.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 15 - Curve the wing using top view
snippet.description: In this step you will create the shape of the wing using the top orthographic view. It's now starting to look like a Spitfire!

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 14 - Add vertices to the wing using insert edge loop
snippet.description: In this step you will use the insert edge loop tool to add vertices to the newly formed wing. This prepare the wing to be curved in the next step.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 13 - Shape the wing using the front view
snippet.description: In this step you will use the front orthographic view to position and shape the newly created wing.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 12 - Extrude the front wing
snippet.description: In this step you will first shape the new faces into the silhouette of a wing and then extrude these faces to create the front wing.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 11 - Use extrude to create faces for the front wing
snippet.description: In this step you will use extrude to create the faces which will become the front wing

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 10 - Prepare to extrude the front wing
snippet.description: In this step you will prepare the mesh in a way that will allow you to successfully extrude the front wing.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 9 - Combine mesh and model the plane in the top view
snippet.description: In this step you will first combine both sides of the mesh. You will then model the shape of the Spitfire using the top view. The plane will be starting to take shape by the end of this step.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 8 - Using insert edge loop to add vertices
snippet.description: In this step you will check the placement of your vertices before adding a few more using the insert edge loop tool.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 7 - Box model the Spitfire in the side view
snippet.description: In this step you will put the mesh into x-ray mode. You will then use the move and scale tools to trace the outline of the Spitfire in the side view.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 6 - Delete half the fuselage and duplicate an instance
snippet.description: In this step you will delete half of the fuselage and create an instance of the other side. This means that you will only have to work on half of the plane which will ensure that the finished plane is symmetrical. This will also save loads of time.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 5 - Edit subdivisions for the fuselage cylinder
snippet.description: In this step you will set the subdivisions for the fuselage.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 4 - Create and position cylinder for fuselage
snippet.description: In this step you will create and position a cylinder. In the next few videos you will manipulate this cylinder to create the Spitfire.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 3 - Positioning image planes
snippet.description: In this video you will make sure that the image planes that contain the reference images are all correctly aligned and to scale.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 2 - Import image planes
snippet.description: In this video you will import reference images as image planes. This will allow you to trace the shape of the plane as we move through the exercise. You will also look at to select image planes in this video.

snippet.title: Maya 2013 intermediate modelling - Spitfire - 1 - Set up
snippet.description:
In this project you will learn more advanced modelling techniques which will allow you to model a Supermarine Spitfire. In this step you will take care of everything you need to do to set up the project for this exercise.

Download the reference images from here: https://docs.google.com/folder/d/0B4hc2Vu6nz34Ty1GOXp3VEFqYVE/edit

Follow this link to learn how to get Maya for free - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n_SjClie5bw

snippet.title: Response to kidfirerock's Maya model problem
snippet.description: The trick is to select all of the objects and then select mesh - combine and then rotate the model into position.

snippet.title: Learn Maya: The basics -- Completed tutorial
snippet.description: This video shows a rendered version of the completed tutorials. Does yours look better than this one? Post a video reply to share your version of the project!

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 13 -- Batch render to a video (avi)
snippet.description:
If you do not want to render to images you can choose to render to video (.avi format on Windows)

Use full frames (uncompressed) for best results.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 12 -- Previewing a batch render using Fcheck
snippet.description: In this step you will use Fcheck to preview the 10 frame animation that you produced in the last step.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 11 -- Batch rendering a scene
snippet.description: In this step you will change some of the render settings to allow you to produce a batch render of your scene. You will then create a test render (10 frames) which you will preview in the next step.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 10 -- Use the graph editor to smooth the in and out tangents (plateau)
snippet.description: In this step you will use the graph editor to smooth the in and out points of the animation curves for the camera. This will make the beginning and end of the animation smoother.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 9 -- Animating a camera using keyframes
snippet.description: In this step you will set two keyframes on your camera to create a panning shot with a little tilt.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 8 -- Working with the camera group and aim
snippet.description: In this step you will use the camera group (found in the outliner) to manipulate the camera and the aim into position.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 7 -- Create a new camera
snippet.description: In this step you will create a new camera. You will create a camera and aim one and this will be used to create an animated panning shot of your scene.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 6 -- Creating a playblast
snippet.description: In this video you will create a playblast of the animation you have created. A playblast is a preview of the animation.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 5 -- Use the graph editor set infinity to linear (make it loop)
snippet.description:
In this step you will use the graph editor to make the animation you have created continue indefinitely.

Make sure you do this for each planet/group before moving on to the next video.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 4 -- Setting keyframes on the groups and planets using "key selected"
snippet.description: In this step you will set the animation for the planets for the first 20 frames. You will use key selected to ensure that the planets only rotate on one axis.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 3 -- Remove animation & set up solar system for animation
snippet.description: In this video you will remove the animation from the sun. You will then add each of your planets to a group which will allow you to have greater control over what is animated.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 2 -- Understanding keyframe animation
snippet.description: In this video you will first change the default in and out tangents to linear before creating a simple keyframe animation of the planets moving around the sun.

snippet.title: Learn Maya 2015: Animation - 1 -- Setting Maya up for animation
snippet.description:
In this series of videos you will animate a solar system and a camera. The scene is based on an earlier modelling tutorial which can be found here - http://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL6AE79443CAB02053
Or you can download the project from here - http://onlinemediatutor.blogspot.co.uk/p/blog-page.html - The download is free but you will be asked to give a social post about the tutorial you are following.

In this first video you will set Maya up for animation.

Learn how to get Maya for free here - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n_SjClie5bw
